section: Decline of the Mughal Empire - causes and historiography; the Later Mughals; regional successor states
subsections: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate
Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers

accepted.s: Bahadur Shah I, who succeeded Aurangzeb, is also known by which epithet?
accepted.x: Bahadur Shah I, also known as Muazzam, was given the epithet Shah-i-Bekhabar.
accepted.tq: Use direct epithet recall and distinguish it from the epithets of later Mughal rulers.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Jahandar Shah:
1. He was known by the epithet ‘Lampat’.
2. He was supported by Wazir Zulfiqar Khan.
3. He ruled under the influence of Lal Kunwar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Jahandar Shah was called Lampat, was backed by Zulfiqar Khan and remained under the sway of his mistress Lal Kunwar.
accepted.tq: Combine three closely related facts about one ruler and identify the complete set.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Jahandar Shah met which fate after his brief reign?
o: He was deposed and killed by Farrukh Siyar and the Sayyids.
He was exiled to Rangoon after the Revolt of 1857.
He was blinded and pensioned by the Company.
He died in office after appointing a successor.
accepted.x: Jahandar Shah was deposed and killed by Farrukh Siyar and the Sayyid brothers.
accepted.tq: Test the fate of a ruler through a person-and-event association.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Farrukh Siyar issued the farman favourable to the English East India Company in which year?
accepted.x: Farrukh Siyar issued the important farman granting favourable trading privileges to the Company in 1717.
accepted.tq: Use numerical discrimination among closely spaced years in the Later Mughal period.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the fate of Farrukh Siyar?
o: He was murdered by Imad-ul-Mulk in 1759.
He was blinded, deposed and killed by the Sayyids in 1719.
He died in office after releasing Shahu.
He was blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla in 1788.
accepted.x: Farrukh Siyar was blinded, deposed and killed by the Sayyid brothers in 1719.
accepted.tq: Distinguish similar violent ends of different Later Mughal emperors.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who among the following was popularly known as ‘Rangeela’?
accepted.x: Muhammad Shah, who ruled from 1719 to 1748, was known as Rangeela.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the ruler associated with a well-known epithet.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad Shah:
1. He got rid of the Sayyid brothers with the help of Nizam-ul-Mulk.
2. Nizam-ul-Mulk, Saadat Khan and Murshid Quli Khan became autonomous during his reign.
3. Nadir Shah invaded India during his reign.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Muhammad Shah eliminated the Sayyid influence with Nizam-ul-Mulk’s help, witnessed the autonomy of major provincial rulers and faced Nadir Shah’s invasion in 1739.
accepted.tq: Check a ruler’s reign through political, provincial and invasion-related facts.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
o: Shah Alam II — Murdered by Imad-ul-Mulk
Alamgir II — Exiled to Rangoon after 1857
Ahmad Shah — Blinded and deposed by Imad-ul-Mulk
Akbar II — Blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla
accepted.x: Ahmad Shah was blinded and deposed by Imad-ul-Mulk. The other fates belong respectively to Bahadur Shah II, Alamgir II and Shah Alam II.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched ruler and fate among closely related Later Mughal events.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Udham Bai, who exercised control during the reign of Ahmad Shah, bore which honorific title?
accepted.x: Udham Bai, who controlled affairs during Ahmad Shah’s reign, was honoured with the title Qibla-i-Alam.
accepted.tq: Test an official title associated with a specific court personality.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following developments took place during the reign of Alamgir II?
o: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 and Abdali invasions continued.
Ram Mohan Roy received the title Raja.
The Third Battle of Panipat was fought and Buxar was won.
The Company granted pension to the first Mughal pensioner.
accepted.x: Repeated invasions by Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Battle of Plassey in 1757 occurred during Alamgir II’s reign.
accepted.tq: Associate events with the correct reign instead of relying only on chronology.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to Shah Alam II, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: He was the first Mughal ruler to release Shahu.
He became the first Mughal pensioner of the Company.
He was killed by the Sayyid brothers in 1719.
He gave Raja title to Ram Mohan Roy.
accepted.x: Shah Alam II became the first Mughal pensioner of the East India Company. He witnessed the Third Battle of Panipat and the Battle of Buxar during his reign.
accepted.tq: Separate the defining political position of Shah Alam II from facts belonging to other rulers.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bahadur Shah II — Exiled to Rangoon after 1857
Shah Alam II — Blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla
Akbar II — Gave Ram Mohan Roy the title ‘Raja’
Muhammad Shah — Exiled to Rangoon after 1857
accepted.x: Muhammad Shah was not exiled to Rangoon. Bahadur Shah II was exiled to Rangoon after the Revolt of 1857; Shah Alam II was blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla.
accepted.tq: Find the mismatched ruler and fate by eliminating well-known correct associations.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Bahadur Shah II, also called Zafar, died in which year after his exile to Rangoon?
accepted.x: Bahadur Shah II was exiled to Rangoon after 1857 and died there in 1862.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of exile-related events from the year of death.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Shah Alam II returned to Delhi under the protection of Mahadji Scindia.
2. He returned to Delhi in 1771–72.
3. Before returning, he lived at Allahabad under Company protection.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Shah Alam II lived at Allahabad under Company protection and returned to Delhi in 1771–72 under Mahadji Scindia’s protection.
accepted.tq: Test a sequence of political circumstances rather than a single isolated date.
accepted.sec: Later Mughals - chronological order, epithets and fate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Murshid Quli Khan held which offices in Bengal?
accepted.x: Murshid Quli Khan first served as Diwan and later became Nazim of Bengal. He ruled Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
accepted.tq: Test the exact office held by a regional founder rather than merely the state associated with him.
accepted.sec: Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Muhammad Khan Bangash — Founder of Hyderabad
Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk — Subedar of Awadh
Ali Muhammad Khan — Nawab of Carnatic under the Nizam
accepted.x: Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk became Subedar of Awadh in 1722 and founded the autonomous state of Awadh.
accepted.tq: Use founder-position matching and reject swaps among successor states.
accepted.sec: Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Carnatic state:
1. Saadatullah Khan is associated with its foundation.
2. The Carnatic was also known as Arcot.
3. Saadatullah Khan named his nephew Dost Ali as successor without the Nizam’s approval.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Saadatullah Khan founded the Carnatic or Arcot state and named Dost Ali, his nephew, as successor without the Nizam’s approval.
accepted.tq: Combine name, alternate designation and succession details in one coded question.
accepted.sec: Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who among the following carved out Rohilkhand during the invasion of Nadir Shah?
accepted.x: Ali Muhammad Khan, an Afghan chief, carved out the state of Rohilkhand during Nadir Shah’s invasion.
accepted.tq: Identify the founder of a regional state through the circumstance of its emergence.
accepted.sec: Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Muhammad Khan Bangash is associated with the foundation of which regional state?
accepted.x: Muhammad Khan Bangash, described as an Afghan adventurer, founded Farrukhabad.
accepted.tq: Direct state-founder recall using nearby regional successor states as distractors.
accepted.sec: Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Person)
a. Husain Ali Khan
a. Murshid Quli Khan
c. Chin Qilich Khan
d. Safdar Jung

List-II (Association)
i. Awadh
ii. Bengal
iii. Sayyid brother
iv. Nizam of Hyderabad

Which of the following is the correct code?
accepted.x: Husain Ali Khan was a Sayyid brother, Murshid Quli Khan was associated with Bengal, Chin Qilich Khan was the Nizam of Hyderabad and Safdar Jung was associated with Awadh.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair and eliminate codes that repeat the wrong regional association.
accepted.sec: Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Sayyid brothers who acted as king-makers during the period 1713–1720 were:
o: Abdullah Khan and Husain Ali Khan
Murshid Quli Khan and Ali Muhammad Khan
accepted.x: The Sayyid brothers were Abdullah Khan, who served as Wazir, and Husain Ali Khan, who served as Mir Bakhshi.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Sayyid king-makers from other powerful nobles of the period.
accepted.sec: Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Sayyid brothers is NOT correct?
o: Husain Ali Khan was the Mir Bakhshi.
They were eliminated during the reign of Farrukh Siyar in 1713.
They dominated Mughal politics from 1713 to 1720.
accepted.x: The Sayyid brothers were eliminated under Muhammad Shah; Husain Ali Khan was killed in 1720. They did not meet this fate during Farrukh Siyar’s reign in 1713.
accepted.tq: Use the NOT format to separate the period of their dominance from the period of their elimination.
accepted.sec: Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the regional successor states is correct?
o: Nizam-ul-Mulk was initially the Subedar of the Deccan and later became Wazir.
Murshid Quli Khan founded Rohilkhand as an Afghan chief.
Muhammad Khan Bangash served as Subedar of Awadh in 1722.
Saadat Khan founded Bengal as its Diwan.
accepted.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk held the position of Subedar of the Deccan and later became Wazir. The other statements interchange the founders and offices of Bengal, Rohilkhand and Awadh.
accepted.tq: Test the position held by the founder and trap office-state reversals.
accepted.sec: Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Awadh succession:
1. Safdar Jung was the nephew and son-in-law of Saadat Khan.
2. Safdar Jung became Nawab of Awadh and Wazir.
3. Shuja-ud-Daula, who came later, fought at the Battle of Buxar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Safdar Jung succeeded Saadat Khan in the specified family relationship and offices, and Shuja-ud-Daula later fought at Buxar.
accepted.tq: Test succession through relationship, office and a later military event.
accepted.sec: Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the early development of Hyderabad?
o: It was first envisaged by Zulfiqar Khan, who governed through Daud Khan from 1708.
It was created by Ali Muhammad Khan during Abdali’s first raid.
It was founded by Murshid Quli Khan after the Battle of Buxar.
It was first envisaged by Saadat Khan as a province of Awadh.
accepted.x: Hyderabad was first envisaged by the Deccan viceroy Zulfiqar Khan, who governed through Daud Khan from 1708.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the initial conception of a state from the later founder traditionally associated with it.
accepted.sec: Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Nizam-ul-Mulk’s administration is correct?
o: He made Puran Chand his Diwan and followed a Mughal-type jagirdari administration.
He made Dost Ali his successor without the Nizam’s approval.
He governed Bengal through Murshid Quli Khan.
He abolished the jagirdari system and appointed Saadat Khan as Diwan.
accepted.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk was tolerant, appointed Puran Chand as his Diwan and administered Hyderabad through a Mughal-type jagirdari system.
accepted.tq: Apply administrative clues to identify the correct regional ruler.
accepted.sec: Regional successor states → founder and position held; Sayyid brothers as king-makers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Nadir Shah defeated the Mughal forces under Muhammad Shah at which place?
accepted.x: Nadir Shah defeated Muhammad Shah at the Battle of Karnal in 1739 before sacking Delhi.
accepted.tq: Match the invader with the decisive battlefield and avoid swapping it with later battles.
accepted.sec: Invasions → invader, year, consequence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the consequence of Ahmad Shah Abdali’s invasions?
o: Bengal and Bihar were ceded to him after the Battle of Karnal.
Punjab and Multan were ceded to him, and he repeatedly invaded during Alamgir II’s reign.
He established the autonomous state of Hyderabad with Puran Chand as Diwan.
He carried away the Peacock Throne after defeating Muhammad Shah at Karnal.
accepted.x: Punjab and Multan were ceded to Ahmad Shah Abdali, and his repeated invasions occurred during the reign of Alamgir II. The other options describe Nadir Shah’s actions or Hyderabad’s administration.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the consequences and identities of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali.
accepted.sec: Invasions → invader, year, consequence  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The invasions of Ahmad Shah Abdali exposed the military weakness of the Mughal Empire.
Reason (R): They repeatedly challenged Mughal authority and drained the imperial treasury.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and the repeated invasions, military challenges and financial drain explain why Mughal weakness was exposed.
accepted.tq: Test whether the stated consequence logically explains the political impact of repeated invasions.
accepted.sec: Invasions → invader, year, consequence  [APPSC]
